newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bank union threatens strike over sick pay.
newsitem.headline: German bank union threatens strike over sick pay.

text.p: German retail, banking and insurance union HBV on Thursday threatened banks with strikes if they carried out their plan to implement a cut in sick pay following a recent change in labour laws.
A union spokesman said the HBV was "outraged" at the banking employers' announcement earlier on Thursday that the cut would come into force for bank workers on October 1 or November 1 at the latest.
If employers stood by their position, "then all signs point to a conflict," the spokesman said in response to a Reuters enquiry.

A spokesman for the Association of German Bank Employers had said the existing wage agreement for the banking sector stated that sick pay arrangements should be determined by whatever legislation currently applied.
A whole array of top German companies including industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG have announced they plan to cut sick pay to 80 percent of normal pay beginning on October 1.
That has fuelled a heated debate over whether the cut, part of new austerity legislation to boost employment and curb government spending, can be applied to existing wage contracts.
